title: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society - Business Studies - Entrepreneurial Skill: Business Opportunity
exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An identified gap in the market or a favorable set of circumstances that creates a need for a new product or service is defined as a:
questions.explain: A **Business opportunity** is essentially an unmet need or a gap in the market that an entrepreneur can profitably fill by providing the right goods or services.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The process of matching a perceived consumer need with the resources required to satisfy that need profitably is the core of identifying a:
questions.explain: Identifying a **business opportunity** requires recognizing what consumers lack and successfully matching it with the resources (capital, labor, materials) to produce a solution at a profit.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: According to the scope and reach of a market, business opportunities are generally classified into the following types **EXCEPT**:
questions.explain:
Based on the BECE syllabus, business opportunities are grouped by geographical scope:

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| **Local** | Within a town, village, or community. |
| **National** | Across the entire country. |
| **International** | Crossing national borders into other countries. |

*Interpersonal* relates to relationships between people, not the geographic scope of a business opportunity.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: An opportunity to set up a small grocery store to serve the immediate daily needs of residents within a specific housing estate is classified as a:
questions.explain: A **Local business opportunity** satisfies the needs of a restricted geographical area, such as a single neighborhood, community, or town.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A business idea that targets consumers and involves the distribution of goods across all the 36 states within Nigeria is classified as a:
questions.explain: Because the operations, market, and logistics span across the entire country (Nigeria), it falls squarely under the classification of a **National business opportunity**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A Nigerian entrepreneur who identifies a high demand for locally processed cocoa in European countries and decides to export is exploring an:
questions.explain: When a business extends its reach beyond its home country to sell goods or services to foreign nations, it is exploiting an **International business opportunity**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: What is the primary factor that distinguishes an international business opportunity from a national business opportunity?
options: The involvement of cross-border trade and differing national currencies.
The amount of profit declared at the end of the financial year.
The number of temporary workers employed by the business.
The use of technological equipment in the production process.
questions.explain: The distinguishing feature of **International trade** (and thus international business opportunities) is the crossing of sovereign national borders, which usually involves dealing with foreign exchange (different currencies), tariffs, and varying international trade laws.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Identifying a shortage of clean drinking water in a specific rural village and deciding to establish a borehole and water packaging enterprise there is an example of exploiting a:
questions.explain: Since the problem identified and the business created are constrained strictly to the *specific rural village*, this is a prime example of finding and utilizing a **Local business opportunity**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When an enterprise successfully plans to expand its operations from selling goods strictly within Nigeria to establishing retail branches in Ghana and South Africa, it is making a transition from a:
questions.explain:
> **Transition Path:**
> 1. Operating strictly within Nigeria = **National**
> 2. Expanding to Ghana & South Africa = **International**

Therefore, the business is scaling its scope from a national presence to taking advantage of an international opportunity.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies
